title: Magnetism and Electromagnets
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Magnetism and Electromagnets Worksheets (Poles, Fields, Electromagnets)
standard_text: Magnetic poles, attraction and repulsion; magnetic fields by plotting with compass, representation by field lines; Earth's magnetism, compass and navigation; the magnetic effect of a current, electromagnets, D.C. motors (principles only).
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on magnetism: poles, magnetic materials, field lines, compasses, electromagnets, how to make them stronger and their uses. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.
key_sub: A current makes a magnetic field; more turns, more current and an iron core make it stronger.
body_html:
How to think about it

Magnets have north and south poles: like poles repel, unlike poles attract.

  • Field lines go from north to south and are closest where the field is strongest.
  • A current in a wire makes a magnetic field. A coil with a current is an electromagnet.
  • More turns, a bigger current and an iron core make an electromagnet stronger.
Example

North pole near a south pole?

Unlike poles

Answer: attract

Example

Remove the iron core: electromagnet?

Iron concentrates the field

Answer: weaker

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all metals are magnetic.
  • Drawing field lines from south to north.
  • Thinking an electromagnet works with the current off.

faq.a: Iron, nickel, cobalt and steel. Most other metals, such as copper and aluminium, are not.

faq.q: How do you make an electromagnet stronger?
faq.a: Use more turns of wire on the coil, a bigger current, or an iron core inside the coil.
They can be switched on and off, so they are used in scrapyard cranes, door locks, relays and electric bells.
